issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig is not thread-safe; races under concurrent first-use
issues.detail: TritonLoraConfig instances are shared across all concurrent requests via TritonModelMetadata.lora_configs. _create_trtllm_generate_request reads is_registered, loads .npy weights, sends them, and sets is_registered=True with no lock and no happens-before with the backend acknowledging registration. Two concurrent first-time requests both see False, both load and send; conversely, a request can flip the flag to True before a prior in-flight request actually reaches the backend, causing later requests to omit weights when the backend has not yet cached them. If the backend rejects after the flag flipped, there is no recovery. Fix: per-config asyncio.Lock with check-after-acquire, or always send weights (idempotent in the TRT-LLM LoRA cache) and drop is_registered, or extract a separate registration registry with stated invariants.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is unstable across calls/restarts and may collide across models
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 inside _parse_lora_configs and increments per LoRA in dict-iteration order over multi_lora.json across repo_paths. The function is called per-model from _get_model_metadata and may be called more than once (reload/refresh). On a second call the same LoRA name can be assigned a different task_id while the TRT-LLM backend still holds the old task_id; two different LoRAs across model-repo entries can collide on the same small integer; reordering multi_lora.json silently reassigns ids. There is no stated invariant tying (name, weights) -> task_id stably. Fix: server-scoped counter, hash-derived/content-derived id, or an explicit field in multi_lora.json — and document the lifetime/namespace contract with the backend cache.

issues.description: _get_lora_config can NoneType-deref on unknown model_name and contradicts its declared return type
issues.detail: self.model_metadata.get(model_name) returns None silently; the next line dereferences model_metadata.lora_configs, raising AttributeError instead of a ClientError. The signature is annotated `-> TritonLoraConfig` but the function also returns None on the lora_name-is-None / lora_configs-is-None paths, so the declared contract is wrong (Optional). Either assert/raise ClientError on missing metadata and annotate Optional[TritonLoraConfig], or split into two functions with honest contracts.

issues.description: lora_config_path local variable is shadowed inside the loop, breaking the outer binding
issues.detail: Outer scope binds lora_config_path = os.path.join(version_path, 'multi_lora.json'). Inside the per-LoRA TRT-LLM branch, the same name is rebound to os.path.join(lora_path, 'model.lora_config.npy'). After the first inner iteration the manifest path is gone, and any subsequent repo_paths iteration that relies on it will silently misbehave. Pike and Dijkstra rate this P0 (silent multi-repo bug class); Knuth/Hickey/Torvalds/Liskov rate it P1 (readability + latent hazard). Either way: rename the inner variable to lora_config_npy_path / lora_adapter_config_path.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` in _parse_lora_configs swallows real errors and returns None, conflating 'no LoRA' with 'failed to load'
issues.detail: The outer try around json.load now also wraps per-LoRA file checks (which raise ServerError, correctly re-raised) plus everything else. A typo producing TypeError, a permission error, an OSError on a network mount, malformed JSON — all are caught, traceback printed to stdout, and the function returns None. The caller treats the model as having no LoRA support at all, silently. Dijkstra rates P0 (DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE); Knuth/Hickey/Torvalds/Liskov/Pike rate P1. Narrow the except to JSONDecodeError/OSError, or raise ServerError with context, or return a tagged result so the caller can distinguish.

issues.description: Synchronous np.load of .npy weights inside async request hot path blocks the event loop
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request calls np.load on model.lora_weights.npy and model.lora_config.npy inside an async coroutine on every cold first-use. For multi-gigabyte LoRA tensors this stalls the event loop, and under the is_registered race may be paid N times. The right shape: load and cache numpy arrays once at _parse_lora_configs time on TritonLoraConfig (as values), and pass by reference at request build time — removing both disk I/O from the async path and the per-cold-request latency spike.

issues.description: O(L) linear scans / list comprehensions used where a dict keyed by name would be O(1)
issues.detail: _validate_chat_request, _validate_completion_request, and _get_lora_config each independently scan metadata.lora_configs (list comprehension `[c.name for c in metadata.lora_configs]`) on every request. Three copies of the same lookup, three places to keep in sync, three list allocations. L is small today, but the data structure for 'lookup LoRA config by name' is a dict — store lora_configs as Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig] (or add a name->config index) and the three call sites collapse to a single dict.get behind one helper. Membership checks should use a set.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs conflates discovery, validation, and side-effectful task-id registration across two backends
issues.detail: What was _get_vllm_lora_names is now a single function with an `if backend == 'vllm': ... else: ...` ladder doing (1) discover names, (2) validate weight/config files exist, (3) allocate monotonically increasing task_ids — for two backends that share almost no code beyond directory walking. This complects discovery (a pure read) with registration state (mutable identity allocation that ought to live in a LoRA registry ADT with documented invariants for restart/eviction). Decompose into _parse_vllm_lora_configs and _parse_trtllm_lora_configs with a thin dispatcher and a separate LoraRegistry for task-id ownership.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig mixes immutable spec with mutable runtime cache state, and conflates backend-specific fields
issues.detail: The dataclass holds name (common to both backends), task_id/path (TRT-LLM-only, optional), and is_registered (mutable runtime registration state). Three concerns in one record: identity (which LoRA), value (weights/config), and time (has the backend cached this yet). Split into a frozen TritonLoraSpec (or backend-specific VllmLoraConfig / TrtLlmLoraConfig with a shared protocol) and a separate registration registry with synchronization. This also removes the is_registered race surface entirely.

issues.description: Backend dispatch in _get_model_metadata silently defaults unknown backends into the TRT-LLM tensor-loading path
issues.detail: The call passes `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend` to _parse_lora_configs. When self.backend is set globally, per-model backend is ignored. Inside _parse_lora_configs, the `if backend == 'vllm': ... else: # assume TRT-LLM` ladder treats ensemble/python backends as TRT-LLM and may blow up on missing .npy files (today it 'works' only because the multi_lora.json check skips them — correct by accident, not reasoning). Make the dispatch explicit (`backend in {'vllm','tensorrtllm'}` else return None), document the precondition tying CLI-declared backend to per-model backend, and reject unknown backends.

issues.description: Stray debug `print(f'backend: {backend}')` left inside the per-LoRA loop
issues.detail: Inside _parse_lora_configs at roughly line 670-684 (depending on which reviewer counted), a debug print fires once per LoRA per model on every metadata refresh. Production servers should not be flooding stdout from a discovery API. Remove, or route through a structured logger at debug level — and if logging is wanted, one line per parse, not one per LoRA.

issues.description: print(traceback.format_exc()) added across three FastAPI routers is logging-by-print, duplicated, and leaks internals
issues.detail: chat.py, completions.py, and embeddings.py each add `import traceback` and `print(traceback.format_exc())` before re-raising ServerError and Exception — three identical copy-pastes that bypass the application logger, log level configuration, structured logging, and log rotation; they also dump tracebacks on every transient backend hiccup and on the embeddings endpoint which has nothing to do with LoRA. Use logger.exception() through a single helper, or remove. Duplication at three sites is its own hazard: someone will fix two of three later.

issues.description: Stale/incorrect return-type annotation on _parse_lora_configs
issues.detail: Signature reads `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but the function returns `Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]`. The annotation is stale from _get_vllm_lora_names. Static analysis and any careful reader is misled; downstream code written against the lying annotation will be wrong. Fix to `Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]`.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered declared `Optional[bool] = False` is a type-annotation lie
issues.detail: is_registered advertises a tri-state (None/True/False) that does not exist anywhere in the code — it is only ever read as a plain bool (`if not lora_config.is_registered`). The Optional is misleading about reachable states. Drop Optional and use `bool = False`, or better, eliminate the field entirely in favor of state that lives where the truth lives (the backend's view of registration). Torvalds extends: same issue for path/task_id, which are required for TRT-LLM and meaningless for vLLM — model that honestly with a sum type or two dataclasses, or a vLLM LoRA can reach _create_trtllm_generate_request and crash on lora_config.task_id being None.

issues.description: PR mixes feature, error-handling, and docs into one patch
issues.detail: This patch ships (1) the multi-LoRA TRT-LLM feature, (2) traceback-print error handling in three FastAPI routers including embeddings (unrelated to LoRA), and (3) a docs rewrite. The router error-handling change is a logging-policy decision that should be reviewed on its own merits, not hidden inside a feature PR. Split into three.

issues.description: TRT-LLM 'first-request-carries-weights' protocol leaks into the frontend request builder
issues.detail: The backend's caching protocol (send lora_task_id + lora_weights + lora_config the first time, lora_task_id alone thereafter) is implementation detail that the OpenAI frontend has now adopted as its own state machine inside _create_trtllm_generate_request. That job belongs in a thin TRT-LLM client adapter that owns the registration cache as a value (a set of task_ids known to the backend), not the request-construction function. The question that should have been asked first: 'whose job is it to know whether the backend has seen this LoRA before?'

issues.description: Test `test_parse_lora_configs` is weak: asserts little about postconditions and shares an expect_error contract across backends
issues.detail: The renamed test calls parse_lora_configs twice (vllm and tensorrtllm) but discards the return value and shares the expect_error contract. TRT-LLM-specific postconditions (ServerError when weights/config files are missing, None when multi_lora.json is absent, monotonically increasing task_ids, correct TritonLoraConfig contents) are unverified — TESTED-NOT-PROVED. Split parametrize entries, assert returned configs, and assert backend-specific behavior.

issues.description: FIXME-tagged `sed` patching of `dims: [ -1, 3 ]` -> `[ -1, 4 ]` in test.sh has no tracked issue or termination condition
issues.detail: The workaround pinned to a TRT-LLM version has no linked upstream issue and no condition for when it can be removed. When TRT-LLM updates, this silently breaks or silently succeeds depending on whether the dims string still exists. Link an issue or pin the TRT-LLM version.

issues.description: Test bifurcation by backend repeats if/elif/else dispatch where a dict table would be smaller
issues.detail: test_lora_separator_not_set, test_lora_separator_set, and test_lora_separator_set_for_lora_off_model each repeat the same `if backend == 'vllm' / elif 'tensorrtllm' / else raise` block. A `{backend: setup_fn}` dict resolved once in setUp removes nine lines of repeated dispatch and makes adding a third backend a one-line change.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig is a class where a dataclass + module-level functions and a separate registration set would do
issues.detail: Data wants to be `{name -> immutable LoraConfig}` plus a separate `{name -> registered?}` set, with two free functions (lookup, mark_registered). Config is data; registration is state; they don't belong in the same struct. That shape is smaller, more obvious, and removes the race window in is_registered.

dissents.topic: Severity of the lora_config_path variable shadowing inside the loop

positions.position: P0 — silent multi-repo bug: outer-scope manifest path is clobbered after the first inner iteration, so any subsequent repo_paths iteration that relies on it will silently misbehave
P1 — readability/structured-programming hazard; reader cannot follow the flow without simulating it
P1 — readability defect literate programming exists to prevent; rename and the bug class disappears
P2 — mechanical, not load-bearing, but a tell that the function is doing too much
P1 — works today because outer with-block is past, but next maintainer will assume same referent
P1 — silently breaks invariant if loop body is extended to reference manifest after first entry

dissents.topic: Severity of the bare `except Exception` returning None in _parse_lora_configs

positions.position: P0 — REFUSED: DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for correctness; conflates JSON-malformed, IO error, permission denied, and KeyError in our own code into 'no LoRA configured'
P1 — invariant contradicted by catch-all; narrow to JSONDecodeError/OSError or propagate as ServerError
P2 — conflates two different facts (no config vs broken config) into one value; return a tagged result
P1 — silently disables LoRA for the model with no signal to operator
P1 — postcondition is now ambiguous; for TRT-LLM where missing weights is a deployment error this becomes load-bearing
P1 — data structure says 'no LoRA here' while side channel says 'something blew up'; pick one

dissents.topic: How to fix the is_registered race

positions.position: Either an asyncio.Lock per TritonLoraConfig with check-after-acquire, or — preferred — always send weights+config (idempotent in TRT-LLM's LoRA cache) and drop is_registered entirely
Extract a separate registration registry keyed by (model, lora_name, task_id) owned by a thin TRT-LLM client adapter; freeze TritonLoraSpec; load weights as values at parse time
Per-config asyncio.Lock, OR send weights every time the engine reports it doesn't know the task_id, OR have the backend confirm registration
Define an explicit LoraRegistry ADT with stated pre/postconditions and invariants; move registration off the request path
Split TritonLoraConfig into {name -> immutable LoraConfig} dict + separate registered-set guarded by a lock; load weights once at parse time

Define the registration protocol as a contract with the backend, state the precondition that is_registered=True means 'backend acknowledged the LoRA tensors for this task_id', and enforce it under concurrency

dissents.topic: Whether the PR should be split into multiple patches

positions.position: Yes — this is three-patches-in-one (feature + router error handling that touches embeddings unrelated to LoRA + docs rewrite); split before merge
Did not raise this; flagged the router prints on their merits but did not call for splitting the PR

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers independently converged on three P0 correctness failures: (1) the is_registered boolean on the shared TritonLoraConfig is mutated from async request handlers with no synchronization, racing under concurrent first-use and breaking the 'first request carries weights' invariant; (2) lora_task_id is assigned per-parse-call in dict-iteration order, so reloads or JSON edits silently reassign ids that the TRT-LLM backend cache still maps to old weights, with no documented namespace contract; (3) _get_lora_config NoneType-derefs on unknown model_name and contradicts its declared non-Optional return type. Universally flagged P1s include: synchronous np.load on the async hot path, three duplicated print(traceback.format_exc()) blocks across FastAPI routers (including embeddings, unrelated to LoRA), stray `print(f'backend: {backend}')` debug in the per-LoRA loop, a stale `List[tuple[str, str]]` return annotation that lies to readers and type checkers, and an O(L) list-comprehension lookup pattern repeated at three call sites where a Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig] would collapse them to one O(1) helper. The strongest preserved disagreements are on severity: Pike and Dijkstra rate the lora_config_path variable shadowing as P0 (silent multi-repo bug class) while the rest rate it P1; Dijkstra rates the bare `except Exception` returning None as P0 (REFUSED, DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE) while others rate it P1-P2; Torvalds is alone in demanding the PR be split into three (feature/error-handling/docs). Reviewers also differ in prescription for the race: lock-based (Torvalds, Knuth alt), idempotent-always-send (Knuth preferred), extract a LoraRegistry ADT (Hickey, Liskov, Pike), or specify the protocol contract with the backend (Dijkstra). NEEDS-WORK / REFUSED across the panel — the algorithm is roughly right but the data structures and invariants have not been stated.
